## Answer

The compressed-air leak was detected on **2025-09-09** (baseline detector, "AIR_LEAK"). MDB-5 is the Compressed Air distribution board.

**MDB-5 energy use:**
| Period | Energy |
|---|---|
| 7 days **before** detection (Sep 2–9) | 20,697.2 kWh |
| 7 days **after** detection (Sep 9–16) | 21,605.2 kWh |

MDB-5 used about **908 kWh more** in the week after detection (≈ +4.4%), which is consistent with the leak keeping the compressed-air system running longer. Note that the leak was already present from 2025-09-03 but only flagged on 2025-09-09, so part of the "before" week already included the leak.

## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

A reflow oven in standby still draws **36% of its 70 kW rating = 25.2 kW** for as long as it is left on [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]. That is a large continuous load producing nothing, so it is the single largest source of weekend idle energy [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Purpose]. A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend (residual heat loss), versus the standby load piling up hour after hour [source: docs/knowledge/equipment/EQ-01_reflow_oven.md#EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual > Energy-saving notes].

The ovens stay on for 30 minutes after the line stops (for heat-up); they must be switched off after that, and only when no boards are inside [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

## Excess energy in incident S5

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-01_energy_policy.md#EM-01 Energy Policy > Objectives > Objective 3: cut idle energy]. The weekend energy was about **1,556 kWh** against about **346 kWh** normal, an excess of about **1,210 kWh** from a single oven [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

Note: the off-schedule rule would only flag this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real saving comes from switching the oven off proactively rather than waiting for detection.

According to SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response, here is the load-shedding order:

**Shed first:** EV charging is the first action — pause EV-01 (100% of its load) [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order].

**Full shed order (stop once projected demand is back under contract):**
1. Pause EV charging — EV-01 (100%)
2. Delay the next burn-in loading — BI-01, BI-02 (35%)
3. Raise chilled-water setpoint +1 degC — CH-01, CH-02 (4%)
4. Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar — AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 (3.5%)

[source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

**Loads that must never be shed:** the server room, running molders mid-cycle, and reflow ovens with boards inside.

[source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]
